newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech state to buy 20,000-30,000T of sugar surplus.
newsitem.headline: Czech state to buy 20,000-30,000T of sugar surplus.

text.p: The Czech state will buy 20,000 to 30,000 tonnes of sugar from the 1996 domestic campaign for its reserves, an Agriculture Ministry official said on Friday.
The ministry and industry sources have said Czechs would have a 50,000 to 100,000 tonne surplus, part of which would go to state reserves while the rest would have to be stored or exported.
"The state will buy 20,000 to 30,000 tonnes for the state reserves," Frantisek Havir, head of the ministry's agricultural production section told Reuters.
He declined to give an exact forecast of the total surplus, saying the information was "sensitive".
"We do not want to move the (domestic) price," Havir said.
Last month the ministry estimated 1996 production at 520,000 to 540,000 tonnes after last year's 460,035 tonnes, implying a surplus of 80,000 to 100,000 tonnes over domestic consumption.
Czech sugar prices are above world levels due to relatively liberal internal market conditions and higher production costs.
The domestic market is protected by a 68.4 percent tariff, which will fall to 65 percent next year.
Industry sources forecast the surplus at 50,000 to 80,000 tonnes. Refiners and traders have said some of the surplus will be stored or exported.

They named Poland, Russia, Ukraine, Bulgaria, Romaina and Saudi Arabia as potential export markets, but added that cheap world sugar would limit export opportunities. --Jan Lopatka, Prague Newsroom 42-2-2423-0003
